title: Tally Votes
prompt: A poll receives one candidate name per vote. Write a function that returns an object where each candidate name maps to the number of votes they received.

explanation.beginner:
Example: tallyVotes(["Ada","Grace","Ada"]) produces {"Ada":2,"Grace":1}. Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Compare “handles no votes”: input [[]] produces {}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Tempting mistake: Reinitializing an existing group erases earlier contributions. Distinct-key counts differ from total occurrences.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles no votes”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
